classification.difficultyReason: The expansion and substitution are specified; subtract the constant term and explain why every remaining integer term has a factor divisible by 9.

content.prompt: By expanding $(1+x)^n$ and substituting $x=18$, show that $19^n-1$ is divisible by $9$.

answer.short:
$9\mid(19^n-1)$.

Substitute $x=18$ into the binomial expansion; every term remaining after subtracting $1$ contains a factor of $9$.
answer.worked:
By the binomial theorem,
$$\begin{align*}(1+x)^n&=1+\binom n1x+\binom n2x^2+\cdots+x^n.
\end{align*}$$
Substituting $x=18$ gives
$$\begin{align*}19^n&=1+\binom n1 18+\binom n2 18^2+\cdots+18^n,\\19^n-1&=18\left(\binom n1+\binom n2 18+\cdots+18^{n-1}\right).
\end{align*}$$
The expression in brackets is an integer, and $18$ is divisible by $9$. Hence $19^n-1$ is divisible by $9$.
